title: ClearLedger
problem_statement: Americans aged 25–40 routinely underestimate their monthly spending by 20–35% because subscription charges, automatic renewals, and recurring transfers are fragmented across 3–5 bank and card accounts with no unified view. Manual budgeting tools fail within two months for 70% of users, and ad-supported apps like Mint prioritize monetization over actionable guidance. As a result, households exceed self-reported budgets by an average of $312 per month while incorrectly believing they are on track, creating compounding financial stress and eroding long-term savings potential.
target_users: Dual-income household managing shared expenses across multiple bank and credit card accounts
Single professional in their late 20s with multiple streaming, SaaS, and gym subscriptions accumulated over time
Freelancer or gig worker with irregular income needing to project whether month-end balances will cover fixed obligations
Recent college graduate transitioning from student loans to full-time income for the first time
Budget-conscious parent tracking household spending across joint and individual accounts
user_stories: As a dual-income household managing shared expenses across multiple bank and credit card accounts, I want a single unified ledger that aggregates all transactions from both partners' accounts so that I can see our true combined monthly spending without logging into four separate portals

As a single professional in their late 20s with multiple streaming, SaaS, and gym subscriptions accumulated over time, I want an automatically generated list of all recurring charges with their amounts, frequencies, and last charge dates so that I can identify forgotten or duplicate subscriptions without manually reviewing twelve months of statements

As a freelancer or gig worker with irregular income needing to project whether month-end balances will cover fixed obligations, I want a month-end balance projection based on confirmed recurring charges and current account balances so that I can take corrective action before overdrafting rather than discovering the shortfall after the fact

As a budget-conscious parent tracking household spending across joint and individual accounts, I want anomaly alerts when a recurring charge increases in amount or a new automatic charge appears on any linked account so that unexpected cost creep does not silently erode our monthly budget

As a recent college graduate transitioning from student loans to full-time income for the first time, I want a clear breakdown of my actual spending by category compared to my self-reported budget estimate so that I can see precisely where and by how much I am overspending each month

As a dual-income household managing shared expenses across multiple bank and credit card accounts, I want read-only bank linking that does not require me to share login credentials directly with the app so that I can grant financial visibility without compromising account security

As a freelancer or gig worker with irregular income needing to project whether month-end balances will cover fixed obligations, I want to receive a mid-month alert when projected month-end balance falls below a threshold I set so that I can prioritize which discretionary expenses to defer
acceptance_criteria: Given a user has linked at least one bank or credit card account via OAuth or tokenized read-only connection, when transactions sync, then all transactions from the past 90 days must appear in the unified ledger within 60 seconds of initial link and within 4 hours of a new transaction posting at the institution

Given the unified ledger contains at least 60 days of transaction history, when the recurring charges detector runs, then it must identify charges that repeat at weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, or annual cadences with the same merchant and a charge amount within plus or minus 2% of the prior instance, and surface them in a dedicated Recurring Charges view

Given a recurring charge has been identified, when the most recent instance of that charge differs from the previous instance by more than 5% or more than $5 (whichever is greater), then the user must receive an in-app notification and a push notification within 24 hours of the charge posting

Given the user has at least 30 days of transaction history and at least one linked account with a known balance, when the month-end projection is calculated, then it must use the current confirmed balance minus all identified upcoming recurring charges due before month-end and display a projected ending balance with a confidence interval

Given a new automatic charge from a merchant with no prior transaction history in the user's linked accounts posts to any linked account, when the anomaly engine processes it, then an alert must be surfaced in the app within 24 hours labeling it as a new recurring charge candidate

Given the user navigates to the Spending vs. Budget view, when actual spending is compared to the user's self-reported budget, then the view must display the dollar and percentage variance per category and in aggregate for the current calendar month with data no more than 4 hours stale

Given the user has linked accounts using read-only OAuth tokens, when ClearLedger accesses account data, then the app must never store raw bank credentials, must encrypt tokens at rest using AES-256, and must pass an independent OAuth security audit before public launch

Given a user sets a month-end balance alert threshold, when the projected month-end balance drops below that threshold at any daily recalculation, then the user must receive a push notification within 1 hour of the calculation completing

Given a user has been active for 30 days, when the app calculates budget adherence, then the displayed budget overage must be accurate within plus or minus $10 compared to a manual reconciliation performed by a QA analyst using the same raw transaction data

Given the app is in use, when any page in the core ledger or recurring charges flow is requested, then it must load and render within 2 seconds on a mid-range Android or iOS device on an LTE connection for the 90th percentile of users

success_metrics.metric: Mean monthly spending underestimation gap (self-reported budget vs. actual spend) among active users
success_metrics.baseline: $312 per month overage at onboarding based on user-reported budget vs. linked account actuals
success_metrics.target: Reduce to less than $150 per month overage within 90 days of first active use

success_metrics.metric: Day-60 retention rate (percentage of users who open the app at least once in week 8 after signup)
success_metrics.baseline: Industry benchmark for personal finance apps: approximately 25% day-60 retention
success_metrics.target: Achieve 45% day-60 retention within 6 months of public launch

success_metrics.metric: Recurring charge detection recall rate (percentage of true recurring charges correctly identified by the detector, validated against a labeled QA dataset)
success_metrics.target: 95% recall with less than 10% false positive rate within 30 days of launch

success_metrics.metric: Time-to-first-insight (minutes from account link completion to user viewing their first Recurring Charges list)
success_metrics.baseline: Not measured pre-launch; estimated 15+ minutes for manual spreadsheet approach
success_metrics.target: Median under 3 minutes post-account-link for 80% of new users

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of new users who complete account linking and view the unified ledger within their first session
success_metrics.target: 70% of new registrants complete linking and view ledger in session 1 within 3 months of launch

success_metrics.metric: Ad-driven revenue as a share of total revenue
success_metrics.baseline: Mint and comparable apps: 40–60% of revenue from advertising and lead generation
success_metrics.target: 0% — ClearLedger operates on subscription revenue only, validated at launch and maintained through year 1

risks_open_questions: Plaid, MX, or Akoya API outages or pricing changes could degrade data freshness or make unit economics unviable — need a multi-aggregator fallback strategy and contractual SLA before launch

Bank re-authentication requirements (OAuth token expiry, MFA prompts) may break automated sync and reintroduce the friction ClearLedger is designed to eliminate — how frequently do major institutions force re-auth and can silent token refresh cover most cases?

Recurring charge detection false positives (e.g., flagging variable utility bills as anomalies) could erode user trust quickly — what is the acceptable false positive rate and how will users dismiss or correct misclassifications?

CFPB open banking rules (Section 1033 of Dodd-Frank) are still being finalized — regulatory changes could affect data portability rights and aggregator liability; need legal review before public launch

User willingness to pay a subscription fee in a market conditioned by free ad-supported tools is unproven — what price point clears a 40%+ conversion rate from free trial to paid, and what is the minimum feature set required for conversion?
Handling joint accounts and shared finances raises data privacy questions between partners — if one partner links a joint account, does the other partner have a right to be notified or to opt out?

Month-end projection accuracy depends on correctly classifying all recurring charges; if a significant charge is miscategorized as one-time, the projection will be wrong and users may overdraft — what is the liability model and how are corrections surfaced to users?

International or multi-currency accounts are held by a non-trivial share of the 25–40 demographic — will ClearLedger support them at launch or explicitly exclude them, and how will that be communicated during onboarding?
out_of_scope: Bill payment, fund transfers, or any write access to linked bank or card accounts
Manual transaction entry or the ability to add accounts not supported by the chosen data aggregator
Investment account tracking, portfolio performance, or retirement planning features
Credit score monitoring or credit report access
Tax preparation assistance or export to tax software
Budgeting advice, financial coaching, or AI-generated savings recommendations in v1
Support for non-US financial institutions or accounts denominated in non-USD currencies
Native web application — v1 is iOS and Android mobile only
Business or small-business account support — personal consumer accounts only
Couples or family sharing features requiring multi-user access to a single ClearLedger account
